description: Toggle a plugin's enabled state in both the persisted per-plugin config and the live orchestrator. Writes the boolean to profile/config/plugins/<plugin_name>.json (creating the file when absent) and then mutates the running roster: when enabling a plugin already in the live roster, its services are started when it implements the LifecycleManaged protocol; when enabling a plugin that is NOT in the live roster, it is staged, wired (orchestrator_ref and event_bus injected before prepare_for_readiness, matching boot order), and committed via the same atomic single-plugin installer install_plugin_from_path uses — every other already-loaded plugin's instance is untouched, and a failure at any staging phase leaves the whole roster, allowlist, and every pre-existing instance byte-identical; when disabling, the plugin's services are stopped first and the plugin is removed from the live roster (orchestrator.plugin_manager.plugins) — dispatch resolves a process key to a live instance by roster lookup, so removal is what makes the plugin's action keys undispatchable. The verb also refreshes the process registry via knowledge_service::refresh_plugin_processes on disable, but that call only re-syncs the plugin's on-disk process-JSON metadata against the knowledge base; it does not itself deregister anything from the runtime dispatch table (that deregistration step belongs to the atomic installer's remove primitive, which this verb's disable path does not call). The persisted boolean survives a solet restart, so a single call makes the enable/disable decision both immediate and durable. The verb does NOT delete the plugin's Python module from sys.modules — re-enabling reuses any already-loaded module objects, only re-instantiating the plugin class. Returns restart_required=true only when the enable path's staged install discovers the plugin's entry-point is not installed at all, or when the entry-point exists but is excluded by the solet's profile manifest allowlist (the staged install never bypasses that exclusion to load an unlisted plugin); the disable path always applies in-process.
embedding_description: Toggle a plugin enabled/disabled live without restart. Writes the bool to profile/config/plugins/<plugin>.json AND mutates the runtime roster: stop_services + drop from the live roster on disable, which is what makes its process keys undispatchable; on enable, an absent plugin is staged, wired, and atomically committed without touching any other loaded plugin's instance. Returns restart_required=true when enabling a plugin whose entry-point is not installed, or one that is installed but excluded by the profile manifest (use install_plugin_from_path or edit the manifest respectively).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Toggle result with keys: applied (bool, true when the runtime state change took effect this session), restart_required (bool, true when only the persisted change took effect and a restart is needed to fully apply), plugin_name (str), message (str status detail).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: On a successful disable, confirm the plugin's services were stopped and it left the live roster — its process keys now fail dispatch because dispatch resolves by roster lookup, not because the registry refresh removed anything. On a successful enable, confirm services are started and process keys are visible. If restart_required is true, surface the reason — the plugin's entry-point is not installed, or it is installed but excluded by the profile manifest — so the caller knows whether to install_plugin_from_path or edit the manifest, rather than defaulting to install in both cases.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a successful disable, do not invoke the plugin's process keys again in the same flow; the plugin instance left the live roster so dispatch will fail. After a successful enable, list_plugins can confirm the new status and process_count. If restart_required is true because the entry-point is missing, install_plugin_from_path is the in-session path to bring it online; if it is true because the manifest excludes the plugin, edit the profile manifest instead — installing will not help. Otherwise, on a router-carrying profile, restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin so the swap is blue-green-safe rather than a bare launchctl restart.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Toggle a plugin on or off in both persisted config and the live orchestrator's roster
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: plugin_name was empty or enabled was not a bool. ConfigManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's config manager attribute is missing (indicates startup did not complete). PluginManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's plugin_manager attribute is missing. LifecycleStartFailure: start_services raised during the enable path; the plugin's services may be in an inconsistent state. LifecycleStopFailure: stop_services raised during the disable path; the plugin's services may not have shut down cleanly. PluginInstallError(phase=contract_validation): enabling a not-yet-loaded plugin staged its class but the instance failed contract validation — the live roster, allowlist, and every other loaded plugin are untouched. PluginInstallError(phase=wiring): enabling a not-yet-loaded plugin staged and instantiated it but prepare_for_readiness/initialize/start_services raised during wiring — same untouched-roster guarantee; the staged instance never reached the live roster.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For missing plugin_name: provide the entry-point name. For unavailable manager errors: do not retry — the platform is in an inconsistent startup state and a restart is the correct recovery. For LifecycleStart/StopFailure: inspect logs for the underlying cause (config drift, missing dependency, port collision) before retrying. For PluginInstallError at contract_validation or wiring: the failure is isolated to the one plugin being enabled — read the named phase and underlying message, fix the plugin (missing dependency, bad config, a raise in prepare_for_readiness/initialize), and retry set_plugin_enabled; no other plugin was affected and no restart is needed. On a router-carrying profile, prefer apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin over a bare restart for any recovery that does need one.
